questions.question: "Stereotactic" biopsy is the preferred method for sampling which of the following findings?
choices: A large solid mass seen on ultrasound
Suspicious microcalcifications or asymmetries NOT seen on ultrasound
questions.detail: Stereotactic biopsy uses X-ray triangulation to localize and sample findings that are mammographically visible but sonographically occult.

questions.question: Which biopsy technique is considered the "gold standard" for sampling highly suspicious clusters of microcalcifications?
questions.detail: Vacuum-assisted devices allow for the collection of large-volume tissue samples, ensuring the calcifications are accurately retrieved.

questions.question: A "Discordant" radiology-pathology correlation occurs when:
choices: The biopsy confirms the suspicious imaging finding
The imaging is highly suspicious (BI-RADS 4/5) but the pathology is benign/non-specific
The patient chooses a second opinion
The biopsy clip is not seen on post-procedure films
The pathology is malignant as expected
questions.detail: Discordance requires a repeat biopsy or surgical excision to ensure the target was not missed during the initial procedure.

questions.question: Why is surgical excision often recommended after a core biopsy diagnosis of "Atypical Ductal Hyperplasia" (ADH)?
choices: There is a 10–20% risk of "upgrading" to DCIS or invasive cancer in the surgical specimen
ADH is contagious to the other breast
questions.detail: Core biopsy only samples a small area; the surrounding tissue in a full excision may contain adjacent malignancy.

questions.question: "Wire Localization" or "Seed Localization" is performed to:
choices: Guide the surgeon to a non-palpable lesion on the day of surgery
Measure the depth of the pectoralis muscle
questions.detail: These markers are placed by the radiologist to ensure the surgeon can accurately remove the correct area of tissue.

questions.question: MRI-guided biopsy is indicated when a suspicious lesion is:
choices: Seen on mammography, ultrasound, and MRI
questions.detail: If a lesion has a correlate on ultrasound, US-guided biopsy is preferred because it is faster, more comfortable, and less expensive.

questions.question: In breast imaging, "Fine Needle Aspiration" (FNA) is primarily used for:
choices: Draining symptomatic cysts or sampling suspicious axillary lymph nodes
questions.detail: FNA provides cytology (cells), which is sufficient for nodes or cysts but lacks the architectural information needed for primary breast masses.

questions.question: Following any percutaneous breast biopsy, the standard of care requires the placement of a:
questions.detail: Clips are essential for "radiology-pathology correlation," identifying the site for future surgical localization, and monitoring the site on follow-up imaging.
